title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 19, 2026
headline: Walt (likely Walter Nolen) is dealing with an ankle issue and an update is due Wednesday or Thursday. Bam Knight impressed in a fill-in run role, 13 personnel with tight ends (Higgins, Quitoriano, McBride) is growing, and red zone run efficiency is the main offensive problem.
summary: LaFleur said the team is a missed field goal away from a very different mood, and that he coaches the same way win or lose. He praised the defensive performance as unified and aggressive, comparing it to 2024, and said Josh Sweat was a force on the edge with production. The offense moved the ball well between the 20s and held the ball for long drives, but was not efficient running in the red zone and settled for six field goals. He said he will clean up the red zone issues and some downhill direct runs, and noted the pin-and-pull runs have been a good change-up. He is using more 13 personnel, which has helped, with Elijah Higgins getting more run, Teagan Quitoriano scoring two touchdowns the week before, and Trey McBride's skill set also valuable. He was complimentary of Bam Knight stepping in (ran hard, tough), while saying the run game still has a lot to clean up. Garrett Williams has moved to safety because of injuries and is handling it well. He said he has moved on to Denver, whose defense he expects to make things very difficult.

injuries.detail: Asked about his ankle (named only as 'Walt'); LaFleur said he'd know more and give an update Wednesday or Thursday.

signals.claim: Bam Knight stepped in and ran hard in Sunday's game and remains a useful contributor in the run game.
signals.note: Knight earned praise for his Sunday performance, which could help him keep a role in the backfield, though the coach did not commit to anything specific.
signals.quote: He's a stud. He's a tough dude.

signals.claim: Higgins will continue to see a bigger role in 13 personnel packages.
signals.note: Increased tight end usage in 13 personnel gives Higgins a growing role.
signals.quote: I thought you saw a little bit more with Elijah.

signals.claim: Quitoriano remains part of the 13 personnel tight end group after his two-touchdown game the week before.
signals.note: Tight end usage is spread across several players, so his role is touchdown-dependent.
signals.quote: Teagan had the two touchdowns the week before.

signals.claim: McBride's skill set will keep being used in both the run and passing game within more 13 personnel looks.
signals.note: Heavy tight end formations should keep McBride involved in the offense.
signals.quote: I think you guys all know what Trey can do.

signals.claim: Sweat is producing as a force on the edge for the defense.
signals.note: Edge production matters for IDP formats; the defense is trending up.
signals.quote: he was a force on the edge there.

signals.claim: Williams will continue playing safety due to injuries at the position.
signals.note: Positional move matters for IDP; he is handling the transition well.
signals.quote: he's doing a good job back there

topics.detail: The offense was not efficient running the ball inside the 20, leading to six field goals. LaFleur said the team was around 13th in red zone ranking coming in and expects to fix it, with play calling constrained by the short field.
Pin-and-pull perimeter runs have been a good change-up, a concept LaFleur used in San Francisco in 2019. Downhill direct runs need cleanup, and the staff discussed different ideas.

LaFleur praised the unified, aggressive play style, compared it to 2024, and said he has a lot of faith in the defensive coordinator and staff. He kept the specifics of the week's adjustments private.
LaFleur took blame for a penalty on a late play call on a screen. Long drives, including two of over eight minutes, are becoming the team's identity, though he still wants more explosive plays.

The kicker made six field goals, and LaFleur credited the operation (snap, hold, protection). He also discussed a defensive lineman's return attempt on a two-point conversion and said it would be addressed in a Friday situation meeting.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Monday, October 19th | Press Conference
headline: AJ Terrell is trending toward coming off IR this week, Kendal Daniels is okay after a hospital trip, and Cooper Rush is out of the QB room after the team added Andy (a QB not on the roster list).
summary: Stefanski opened with good news on Kendal Daniels, who went to the hospital during the Week 6 loss to Chicago but is back in the building. He had no game-status updates on Daniels or anyone else because imaging is still pending on several players. He said Atlanta dug itself a hole, falling behind 31-7 in the fourth quarter, and he put the blame on coaches and players across offense, defense and special teams. He said the team did not make Chicago pay enough for pressure and blitzes on Michael Penix Jr., and that the pass rush and coverage have to work together. The team added a QB named Andy and moved on from Cooper Rush, though Stefanski did not describe the exact transaction. Andy is still learning names and the system, and Stefanski would not say where he slots in the QB depth chart. AJ Terrell's IR window opens, and activation is trending that way. Stefanski gave Mike Hughes a vote of confidence but said the corner spot will be reviewed this week. He praised Jahan Dotson as a trusted receiver, and said the game script forced tempo and cut into the run game. San Francisco is the next opponent, at home.

injuries.detail: Went to the hospital during the game but returned to the locker room that night and was in the building Monday. Stefanski feels good about where he is but gave no update on his availability for next week.
His IR return window opens this week. Activation and practice are 'trending that way,' but the team will wait a few days.

signals.claim: Terrell will be activated from IR or start practicing this week.
signals.note: His return would boost the Falcons' secondary and could change the cornerback rotation.
signals.quote: it's trending that way, Daniel.

signals.claim: Daniels is recovering well, but his availability for the next game is not yet known.
signals.note: Check the injury report this week, since his game status depends on pending imaging.

signals.claim: The cornerback alignment will be reviewed this week, including once AJ Terrell returns.
signals.note: Hughes could lose snaps if Terrell returns or the team makes a change after he gave up many passing yards.
signals.quote: Obviously Mike's a vet that we're counting on.

signals.claim: The offense will work on handling heavy pressure and blitzes after Penix faced a career-high pressure rate.
signals.note: Opponents may copy Chicago's blitz-heavy approach, which could hurt Penix's efficiency and the passing game.
signals.quote: we didn't do that enough yesterday.

signals.claim: Dotson will keep a trusted role in the passing game, including on downfield and end-zone targets.
signals.note: He is a trusted secondary receiver with big-play ability who could keep getting chances behind the top weapons.
signals.quote: He does a lot of different jobs for us and he's somebody that we trust.

signals.claim: Robinson's run-game involvement drops when the team has to play from behind in tempo mode, and should rise with a more balanced game script.
signals.note: His touches depend on game script, and trailing early cuts into his rushing volume.
signals.quote: It takes the run game out of it a little bit.

signals.claim: Rush is no longer on the active QB depth chart after the addition of Andy.
signals.note: It is a backup QB roster change with little immediate fantasy impact, but it does reshape the QB room.
signals.quote: obviously, I think the world of Cooper Rush

topics.detail: Stefanski said the team put itself in a hole against Chicago, with slow starts including two three-and-outs early. He placed the blame on everyone and said they must be honest about it on tape.
Chicago's screens, keepers and offensive line gave the Falcons trouble. He said the rush and coverage must work together and that fully shutting down that offense is not realistic.

Newly added QB Andy is still learning names and the system, and his place in the depth chart behind Penix, including against Tua Tagovailoa, is undecided. Jack Strand's situation is unaffected by the addition.

Atlanta plays a very good San Francisco team at home, and Stefanski plans to start in-depth work on the 49ers soon. He noted that opposing coach Raheem Morris knows the Falcons' roster, as every week features some familiarity.

title: Jesse Minter on Browns Loss, Lamar Jackson's Status
headline: Lamar Jackson is day-to-day with Wednesday the key update, Ja'Kobi Lane impressed in his return, and Bateman and Hendrickson both appear to have come out of the loss in decent shape.
summary: Minter called the Week 6 loss to Cleveland a disappointing game the Ravens let slip. He said they failed to separate after halftime and gave a good team chances to hang around, and he put it on the team. Lamar Jackson is still day-to-day, with more clarity expected Wednesday, and Minter said Jackson could potentially practice this week. Minter said Cleveland's defense hurt the offense by attacking the run game with downhill linebackers and aggressive man coverage, which took Derrick Henry away after two good opening drives. He praised Ja'Kobi Lane's physical catches and blocking in his first game back and expects him to improve as he gets into rhythm. Keyon Martin returned to the dime role over Chandler Rivers, and Minter said Martin played well. Trey Hendrickson came out of his first game back in good shape, and Rashod Bateman had a minor issue but there is optimism he'll be fine. A player referred to as "Kim Jordan" (not clearly identifiable) is progressing through concussion protocol and could return this week. Minter was noncommittal on the kicker position after more misses, saying the team is always looking at ways to improve the roster. He also said the offensive line has been inconsistent and the team is still chasing improvement there. The next opponent is an unnamed division opponent.

injuries.detail: Day-to-day; more will be known Wednesday. Potentially practices this week, but Minter said "we'll see how it goes."
Played in his first game back, rushed well, and Minter feels good about how he came out. It is still an ongoing situation.
Dealt with something late in the game, but Minter sees a little optimism that he should be okay.

signals.claim: Jackson's availability will be clearer Wednesday and he may practice this week.
signals.note: His Week 7 status is unresolved, so monitor Wednesday's practice report before setting lineups.

signals.claim: Lane should keep getting playing time and take a jump as he gets into rhythm.
signals.note: Minter praised his contested catches and physicality, which could mean a growing receiver role.
signals.quote: hopefully he can now get in rhythm and you'll see some major jumps for him

signals.claim: Bateman should be okay after a minor in-game issue.
signals.note: He looks likely to play, but his practice participation is worth watching.
signals.quote: there's a little bit of optimism that, that, uh, you know, he should be okay.

signals.claim: Opponents will keep trying to take away the Ravens' run game, as Cleveland did.
signals.note: Henry was contained by aggressive run defense, and the offensive line is still inconsistent, so his efficiency is a concern.
signals.quote: they got pretty aggressive to take Derrick in the running game away.

signals.claim: Hendrickson is trending well after his first game back and will keep playing.
signals.note: Relevant for IDP: he is healthy enough to play and the pass rush is improving.

signals.claim: Martin has moved back ahead of Chandler Rivers in the dime package.
signals.note: IDP-relevant: he is back in a nickel/dime role.

signals.claim: The Ravens will move Green and Hendrickson around to maximize both.
signals.note: Playing time and alignment for the edge rushers is still being sorted out, which could affect Green's IDP production.

topics.detail: Cleveland attacked the wide zone run game, got downhill with linebackers, and played aggressive man coverage after the first two drives. Delay-of-game penalties came from operational issues, and Minter said the offensive line was good at times but beaten at others.
Minter said the kicker's second-half misses are as costly as turnovers. He wouldn't rule out bringing in another kicker, saying the team is always looking to improve the roster.

Minter wants a more aggressive, playmaking approach in late-game coverage. He also cited special teams mistakes, including a dropped return and a touchback punt in the final minutes, as missed chances.
A player referred to as "Kim Jordan" is coming along in concussion protocol, and the team is excited to potentially get him back this week. A final decision could come today or tomorrow.

title: Joe Brady Discusses Gardner-Johnson Suspension, Injury Updates, Self Scouting, And More
headline: Bills are on a bye with C.J. Gardner-Johnson suspended by the league; DJ Moore and Ed Oliver are 'close' to returning for Week 8 at Baltimore, and James Cook looks like the featured back despite workload concerns.
summary: Brady called Gardner-Johnson's ejection and league suspension inexcusable. He said it was addressed privately and with the team, and that the only punishment is the league's. Gardner-Johnson remains a Buffalo Bill, but Brady framed it as a chance for someone else to step up while he is out, and he did not commit to the starting job. Brady said he is not happy with how the team is playing despite a 5-1 record, citing penalties and fourth-quarter points allowed (17 against the Raiders, 20 against the Rams). He said the bye week will go to self-scouting before Baltimore prep. On injuries, he said DJ Moore and Ed Oliver are 'close', and the hope and intent is for them to be back next week. Moore's absence has made game planning uncertain, but Keon Coleman made plays when his chances came, and Josh Allen stayed calm and protected the ball. Brady praised James Cook's ball security, said he would give him the ball, and said he must be mindful of Cook's workload for the long haul. He also praised the special teams (Ray Davis's kickoff coverage, the punter's hang time, and a penalty-free game).

injuries.detail: Has missed recent games; Brady said he is 'close' and the hope and intent is to be back next week after the bye, but it will depend on how this week looks.
Brady said the players are close, with the hope and intent of being back next week, pending how the bye week goes.
Suspended by the league after being ejected for a hit in the Raiders game.

signals.claim: Gardner-Johnson will miss time due to league suspension and others will play in his place; his return role was not guaranteed.
signals.note: Safety snaps open up for others while he is suspended, and Brady did not clearly commit to him as a starter on return.

signals.claim: Moore is close to returning and the intent is for him to be back after the bye in Week 8 at Baltimore.
signals.note: His return would bring back the top target in the passing game and push others down the target pecking order.
signals.quote: the hope and intent with them to be back next week

signals.claim: Oliver is close to returning and is expected to be back after the bye if there are no setbacks.
signals.note: A returning interior defender helps the pass rush and run defense, which matters for IDP and the defense/special teams (DST) unit.
signals.quote: I like to think that they're close.

signals.claim: Coleman has produced when targeted during Moore's absence and should keep seeing opportunities.
signals.note: He is a beneficiary if Moore misses more time, though his target share drops if Moore returns.

signals.claim: Cook will remain the lead back and get the ball, while Brady manages his workload for the long haul.
signals.note: Brady praised Cook's play and said he was going to feed him, but said he is mindful of workload, so a sudden spike in carries is unlikely.

signals.claim: Allen is handling defenses' changing looks and protecting the ball without Moore.
signals.note: His steady play suggests the offense can keep producing even without its top receiver.
signals.quote: Josh not panicking I thought was outstanding.

signals.claim: Davis was an elite contributor on kickoff coverage as an All-Pro special teamer.
signals.note: He gets special teams praise only, with little fantasy value from it.
signals.quote: the first opening kickoffs all pro ray day was outstanding.

topics.detail: Brady said the team is committing too many penalties across offense, defense and special teams, and that Gardner-Johnson's ejection cost field position and a player for the rest of the game. He said the team will toe the line but cannot cross it.
The staff will spend the week on self-scouting, covering tendencies, tape and league trends, before turning to Baltimore, because there is no second bye to do a full-scale review.
The defense gave up 17 fourth-quarter points to the Raiders and had no sacks, but Brady liked the number of quarterback hits and contested balls. He said third-down defense needs work.
Brady called the kickoff coverage elite, with about 12 different players making tackles, and said the punter had elite hang time. The unit was penalty-free and the kicker went four for four.
Brady said he has not thought about the trade deadline and trusts GM Brandon Beane to handle roster decisions.
Defenses are starting to play Buffalo differently, and Brady said the offense must keep evolving. The Raiders missed chances to put the game away, with two field goals in the second half.

title: Dave Canales: 'A man with options is blessed'
headline: Panthers' offense got Taylor Moton back and Tommy Tremble had his best game, but Monroe Freeling's return could reshuffle the tackle spots. Jaelan Phillips' hamstring and calf are being evaluated, with a report due Wednesday.
summary: Canales was happy with a win in Philadelphia built on all three phases. The offense struggled early but finished the game on its own terms with a physical, run-heavy closing drive. The defense held a second straight opponent to 50 rushing yards or fewer, and he credited line fundamentals, edge-setting and the linebackers for that. He was critical mainly of penalties, but called them the product of aggressive play and said he won't back Will Lee off. Taylor Moton played about 80 snaps in his first game back, Tershawn Wharton had splash plays on a limited rep count, and Trevor Etienne improved the punt return game. Monroe Freeling is nearing a return, and Canales laid out a decision with several scenarios, saying the healthiest, best group will play. Rasheed Walker played his best game in Moton's absence. Jaelan Phillips is being checked for the same hamstring and a calf issue. Canales praised Tommy Tremble's best game, took blame for the end-of-half clock management, and said the quarterback for next week's opponent could be Baker Mayfield or Jalen, with a short week before Green Bay.

title: Zac Taylor: "Our Guys Get Really Fired Up For This Game" | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Colbie Young is nearly healthy and set to reclaim his pre-injury role while Tanner Hudson is lost. Erick All's targets are not guaranteed, because Taylor says the whole receiver/TE room will be used.
summary: Taylor spoke after the bye week and looked ahead to a divisional road game at Baltimore, saying the team is excited for it and that turnovers and field position are the key AFC North themes. Safety Kyle Dugger is "progressing along," and Bryan Cook feels much closer to 100% after the bye. A player the transcript renders as "Cassius Powell" (likely Cashius Howell) is sick. With Tanner Hudson out, Taylor said Colbie Young looks the best he has in a long time and can get back into his earlier role. Taylor said Young's skill set overlaps with Hudson's F-tight-end role. Asked whether Erick All would see more targets, Taylor was noncommittal: roles will be spread across the receiver and tight end rooms week to week, and the receiver room is getting healthier. Taylor said the offense's identity is trying to score points on every drive. He said the bye does not change game workload, though practice reps may be managed for veterans. He also recalled the 2021 win in Baltimore, when the team introduced seven-man protection.

injuries.detail: Was back last week; Taylor said he is progressing and the team will see where he is at, with no firm status given.
Transcript says "Cassius Powell"; Taylor confirmed he is sick, with no further detail. Name match is likely but not certain.
Missed a couple of games; feels a lot better coming off the bye and is closer to full strength.
Rehab progressed last week and he moved around well at practice today; Taylor says he is closer to 100% health.

signals.note: A healthy Young could take back snaps and targets as an offensive depth piece, especially with Hudson out.

signals.claim: Targets and passing-game roles will be spread across the receiver and tight end rooms and decided week to week.
signals.note: Taylor praised his physicality after the catch and in the run game but would not promise more targets, so he is a watch-list tight end.
signals.quote: we'll call on the whole room in the receiver room.

signals.note: Losing Hudson removes a pass-catching tight end option and opens opportunity for Young and the other tight ends.
signals.quote: to lose Tanner and get Colby back in some ways does help

signals.claim: Will be closer to full strength for Baltimore and is expected to play a big role in tackling and communication.
signals.note: A healthier Cook helps the secondary against Baltimore's physical backs and mobile quarterback, which matters for IDP and defense streaming.
signals.quote: he feels a lot better than he probably did two weeks ago

signals.note: Taylor gave no firm timeline, so check his practice reports for IDP or defense decisions.

topics.detail: The team travels to Baltimore for a divisional game. Taylor stressed turnovers and field position in AFC North games, and said Baltimore has new schemes but still has great players.
Taylor said he has a good sense of the offense's identity: try to score points on every drive. He also said the goal is to keep getting points on the board with detailed execution.
The early bye does not change game-day workload. The staff may lighten practice reps for veterans to keep them healthy for Sunday.
Taylor praised the new Baltimore defensive coordinator, who previously coached the Chargers, as smart and well respected by players.

title: HC Sean Payton ahead of Week 7: ‘We’ve got a chance to play better this upcoming weekend’
headline: Payton backs Bo Nix and rules out a QB change, blaming the lack of vertical plays on defensive looks, the offensive line and play-calling. He wants more run balance and chunk plays against Arizona in Week 7.
summary: Payton was asked mostly about Bo Nix after a win that left the offense short of explosive plays and Nix visibly frustrated. He said Denver expected a challenging two-high shell and will be able to get the ball downfield. He put the responsibility for creating chunk plays on himself and the coaching staff. Asked about a quarterback change, he said no, as he had a week earlier. He argued Nix's play will improve as a byproduct of better offensive line play and a more efficient, balanced running game. On Nix's frustration and the ankle, he spoke generally about mental toughness and said the body language reflects the offense not getting first downs. He noted the team is 4-2, said attention to detail has to improve, and said the team will play better this weekend. He declined to detail Jonathan Cooper's self-improvement work after the exempt-list situation, and said he is focused on preparing for Arizona rather than national criticism of Nix.

injuries.detail: A reporter asked about a mental hurdle tied to his ankle. Payton did not give a physical status and spoke only about mental toughness.

signals.claim: Nix remains the starting quarterback and Denver will look to create more chunk plays for him, with the offense improving this week.
signals.note: Nix's job is safe for now, but the offense is struggling to push the ball downfield, which caps his and the receivers' upside until it changes.
signals.quote: he's going to become the byproduct of all the the finer things that can improve

topics.detail: Payton tied the offense's improvement to better offensive line play and more efficient, balanced running of the football.
The two-high shell limited downfield throws. Payton said the staff must give players chunk-play opportunities and will get the ball down the field.
Payton said Cooper took steps on his own after the June incident and did not back away from what was necessary. He gave no further detail.

title: Campbell on divisional game
headline: Lions plan to play both Cade Mays and Juice Scruggs on the interior line vs. GB, with the center/guard arrangement still being sorted out. Penei Sewell is praised at left tackle, and a returning player's workload is being managed (name unclear).
summary: Campbell said the bye week brought some clarity on what to do more and less of, and that the team is starting to figure out its identity with some players returning from injury. The Lions open divisional play at home against a Packers team he called good and well coached, and he praised Green Bay's defensive disguises, back-end play and front. He said he plans to play both Cade Mays and Juice Scruggs barring a setback, though they are still deciding how to rotate them at center, where Scruggs has played well and gotten better each week. Scruggs can be kept ready at center and also work at guard, and Christian Mahogany has had a couple of good weeks, which gives the line depth and competition. A returning player (not named in the transcript) won't be asked to handle 70 plays, but the staff believes he can take on quite a bit and will push him in practice before the game. Campbell called Penei Sewell's move to left tackle outstanding and said he looks even smoother and has found another gear. He noted that Josh Jacobs may return for Green Bay, which would add a downhill, explosive element to their run game. He also said the Lions need back-to-back wins and must play better than they did at Arizona.

injuries.detail: Coming back from injury; Campbell plans to play him barring a setback, but how he and Scruggs split time at center is undecided.

signals.claim: Will keep playing and be ready at center, and may also work at guard, as the team sorts out its interior line with Cade Mays back.
signals.note: Scruggs's strong play is forcing the staff to rethink the center job, which matters for Detroit's run-blocking and interior protection.
signals.quote: Juice is playing pretty good football for us right now. He's gotten better every week.

signals.claim: Mays will play this week barring a setback, but his role (center vs. guard) and snap share are undecided.
signals.note: The interior line split is not settled, so his workload is uncertain.

signals.claim: Sewell will remain at left tackle, where he is playing at a high level, and can still move to the right side.
signals.note: A strong left tackle supports Goff's protection and the run game.
signals.quote: he's playing high level football right now at left tackle.

signals.claim: Mahogany has played well recently and remains part of the interior line depth.
signals.note: Role may be affected by how Mays and Scruggs are used.
signals.quote: Mahogany has had a couple of good weeks.

topics.detail: Campbell praised Green Bay's coverage disguises, its safeties and corners, and its front, saying the unit puts a lot of pressure on the offense in a longer down-and-distance game. He compared it to the Bears game.
If Josh Jacobs returns, Campbell expects Green Bay to run the same plays with a more downhill, explosive element, and said Detroit cannot let him get going.
Campbell said the Lions are young and ascending, are starting to find their identity, and need back-to-back wins and a better performance than they gave at Arizona.
The team practices Tuesday instead of Wednesday so it can push players harder before a day off.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'He balled out'
headline: Josh Jacobs is expected to practice fully this week after six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list, with his Detroit workload still to be decided. Jordan Love 'balled out' in the 23-13 win.
summary: LaFleur praised Jordan Love's performance against Dallas, saying he played about as well as he could while taking a lot of hits, and he complained about uneven roughing-the-passer calls. He said Josh Jacobs, after six weeks away from team football activities, should get a full week of practice. How ready Jacobs is, and whether he gets a snap or touch limit at Detroit, will be decided during the week. LaFleur called Jacobs an elite back who can provide a spark for a run game that has struggled. He said run blocking was mixed, partly because Dallas showed fronts the offense had no good plays for, and pass protection had a couple of busts. title: DeMeco Ryans on Tank Dell’s Return, C.J. Stroud & Giants Week
headline: Tank Dell is set to return Sunday vs. the Giants after two weeks of practice, and Foster Moreau and Jawhar Jordan showed up in the win over Jacksonville.
summary: Ryans said the offense runs through C.J. Stroud, who he says is confident, protects the football and spreads the ball around. He confirmed Tank Dell will play Sunday against the Giants after practicing well for two weeks, and said he has no specific expectations beyond Dell being himself and stressing defenders with his speed. Foster Moreau scored twice, including a one-handed catch on a play the team repeated in Friday's practice. Ryans praised the running back group, especially the speed and cutback ability of the back he called 'George' (likely Jawhar Jordan), who had a 25-yard TD and a key toss in the two-minute drill. Marvin Harrison Jr. made his first catch with the team, a contested grab over the middle. On defense, Ryans said the tackling is not good enough and must improve quickly against the Giants' two physical backs. Tremon Smith was named player of the game after two critical stops. title: Shane Steichen: Week 6 recap, Colts vs. Titans
headline: Daniel Jones remains the starting QB, but Sauce Gardner is week-to-week with a calf injury and Alec Pierce won't practice this week while still on IR.
summary: Steichen opened by addressing the firing of GM Chris Ballard. He praised Ballard personally but said the failures don't fall solely on him, and that coaches and scouts share the responsibility. He said his focus is on preparing for the Vikings in Week 7 and he dodged questions about his own job security and possible roster or lineup changes, saying only that the team always evaluates everything. He confirmed Daniel Jones is the starting quarterback and that Lou Anarumo will keep calling defensive plays. Sauce Gardner left the game with a calf injury and is week to week, with his status to be judged by the end of the week. Alec Pierce is eligible to return from IR this week but is still rehabbing and will not practice. The team is 2-4, and Steichen said he told the players they dug the hole together and must climb out together. He stressed blocking out the noise, a sense of urgency and attention to detail. On Jones, he said the quarterback knows he must play better, and he singled out turnovers, especially in the red zone, as the main issue to fix.

title: Liam Coen Speaks Monday after Loss to Texans | Press Conference
headline: Jaguars are on their bye after a 34-31 loss to the Texans. Coen is very pleased with Trevor Lawrence, no one on IR is expected back soon, and TE Nate Boerkircher is earning more run.
summary: Coen spoke the day after the Week 6 loss to the Texans in London, with the bye week next. He said he is very pleased with Trevor Lawrence and the offense's response. The run game was efficient and pass protection was strong, though he wants more explosive runs and said he could have run more if the team hadn't trailed by ten. He credited the offensive line and said the slick Wembley turf favored the offense over the defense. On defense he blamed communication, young players in the back end, and too much scheme inventory. He said Houston's jumbo personnel beat Jacksonville on single-high disguises, the team missed tackles, and it allowed 114 rushing yards, which he called not their standard. In the rookie report he singled out Nate Boerkircher's red-zone play and added snaps, and said Josh Cameron is playing a lot. He also praised Emmanuel Pregnon's interior play. On injuries, he doesn't see anyone coming off IR soon, and Anton Harrison's timeline is unclear. Priorities during the break are situational football (clock, end-of-half scenarios) and cutting self-inflicted penalties.

title: Andy Reid: 'Defensively We Did a Really Nice Job of Executing the Plan' | Press Conference 10/19

title: Andy Reid: 'Defensively We Really Put the Hammer Down' | Postgame Press Conference - NFL Week 6

title: Sean McVay, Tyler Higbee & Quentin Lake discuss injury updates after Week 6, taking accountability, positive takeaways from Sunday & more
headline: Davante Adams is out 6-10 weeks (hamstring/knee rupture) and Kobie Turner is out weeks with a groin strain. Poona Ford and kicker Blake Grupe are done for the season, so the Rams are thin at WR with a kicker signing coming.
summary: McVay opened with the injury list from the Week 6 loss to Arizona. Poona Ford (ruptured triceps) and kicker Blake Grupe (torn ACL on a kickoff tackle) are done for the year. title: Head Coach Jim Harbaugh Postgame Press Conference vs. Chiefs
headline: Chargers fall to 0-6 heading into the bye with the offense struggling; Harbaugh says playcalling and everything else is under review, and Justin Herbert wasn't put in position to succeed.
summary: Harbaugh opened by acknowledging the 0-6 record going into the bye and said he was confident the team would win. His main concern was the offense, which isn't scoring enough points. Asked whether Mike McDaniel will keep calling plays, he didn't commit and said everything will be evaluated, starting with himself and the offensive coaches. He called the missed first-and-goal at the one a very big missed opportunity but wouldn't break down specific plays until he watched the tape. He said the effort in meetings and practice is there but it isn't translating to games across the run, pass and short-yardage game. On defense he pointed to stops and a big red-zone turnover against a highly productive Chiefs operation. About Herbert, he said he didn't get many chances and did everything he could, but from the sideline he felt the offense wasn't putting him in a position to be successful. He rejected injuries as an excuse, said the offense can be fixed, and wouldn't rule out wholesale change.

The team signed a fullback to allow more two-back sets, which Macdonald said is not a comment on Brady Russell.
Macdonald declined to share his philosophy on two-point conversions when trailing by 14.

title: Todd Bowles on Baker Mayfield’s Timeline to Return | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield is expected to practice Wednesday, but Jalen McMillan's name came up as the fallback and Bowles wouldn't commit to a Week 7 starter; David Walker's pass-rush role keeps growing.
summary: Bowles said the Bucs held Pittsburgh well on defense but still failed to finish the game, and that the offense needs to catch up. He blamed the defense's late-game slip on missed assignments and a couple of tackling issues, and said the defense isn't getting enough help from an offense that wasn't moving the ball. He said Baker Mayfield is supposed to practice Wednesday and will be evaluated through the week, and that both quarterbacks will be in the meetings and prepped before a starter is chosen. A'Shawn Robinson lined up on the edge as a bigger body to help against the run, tied to the four-man front question from earlier in the year. Bowles was critical of punter Riley Dixon, saying the team needs more hang time and distance. He said David Walker's role has been ramped up weekly because of his production (four sacks), that he wants more reps for him, but it depends on game plan and personnel. He described Walker as third in the rotation in that specific package. He called the upcoming divisional games, starting with Carolina, critical to getting back in the race.
